title: Set (cited)
primary_statement: A set in ZFC -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:set

title: Function (cited)
primary_statement: A function f: X -> Y as a functional relation -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:function

title: Bijection (cited)
primary_statement: A function that is injective and surjective; has a two-sided inverse -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:bijection

title: Equivalence relation (cited)
primary_statement: Reflexive, symmetric, transitive relation; partitions its underlying set -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:equivalence_relation

title: Quotient set (cited)
primary_statement: X/~, the set of equivalence classes, with the canonical projection -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:quotient_set

title: Finite set (cited)
primary_statement: A set equinumerous with some {1,...,n} -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:finite_set

title: Indexed family (cited)
primary_statement: A function from an index set I into a set, written (x_i)_{i in I} -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:indexed_family

title: Zorn's lemma (cited)
primary_statement: Every nonempty poset in which every chain has an upper bound has a maximal element -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:zorn_lemma

title: Axiom of choice (cited)
primary_statement: Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; equivalent to Zorn -- math-sets-functions-cardinality:axiom_of_choice

title: Induction (cited)
primary_statement: Proof by weak and strong induction on N -- math-logic-and-proof:weak_induction

title: The real field R (cited)
primary_statement: R is a complete ordered field -- math-number-systems:real_number

title: The complex field C (cited)
primary_statement: C = R[i]/(i^2+1), an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0; no capsule in this stack constructs it

title: Fundamental theorem of algebra (cited)
primary_statement: Every nonconstant polynomial over C has a root; C is algebraically closed. Cited, not proved -- no capsule in the stack develops it

title: Compactness of the unit sphere (cited)
primary_statement: The unit sphere in R^n is closed and bounded hence compact -- math-real-analysis:heine_borel

title: Extreme value theorem (cited)
primary_statement: A continuous real function on a compact set attains its supremum -- math-real-analysis:extreme_value_theorem

title: Polynomial ring F[t] (cited)
primary_statement: F[t] with degree, division with remainder, and unique factorisation into irreducibles

title: Field
primary_statement: A commutative ring in which every nonzero element is invertible: (F,+,*,0,1) with 0 != 1

title: Characteristic not 2
primary_statement: 1 + 1 != 0 in F. Required wherever a factor of 1/2 is taken

title: Algebraically closed field
primary_statement: Every nonconstant polynomial in F[t] splits into linear factors over F

title: Ordered field
primary_statement: F carries a total order compatible with + and *; needed to call a scalar positive

title: Finite-dimensionality
primary_statement: V has a finite spanning set. A first-class hypothesis, never ambient

title: Index and shape convention
primary_statement: Vectors are columns; A in F^{m x n} has m rows and n columns; indices start at 1; A_{ij} is row i column j

title: Transpose vs conjugate transpose
primary_statement: A^T is the transpose, A^* the conjugate transpose; they coincide over R. Every Hermitian result says which it uses

title: Inner-product linearity convention
primary_statement: The complex inner product is linear in the FIRST argument and conjugate-linear in the second (the mathematician's convention)

title: Characteristic polynomial sign convention
primary_statement: p_A(t) = det(tI - A), monic. The variant det(A - tI) differs by (-1)^n

title: Vector space
primary_statement: An abelian group (V,+) with scalar multiplication F x V -> V satisfying distributivity, associativity, and 1v = v

title: Elementary consequences of the axioms
primary_statement: 0v = 0, (-1)v = -v, a0 = 0, and av = 0 implies a = 0 or v = 0

title: Subspace
primary_statement: A subset U of V containing 0 and closed under + and scalar multiplication; equivalently a subset that is a vector space under the restricted operations

title: Subspace criterion
primary_statement: Nonempty U is a subspace iff au + bw is in U for all a,b in F and u,w in U

title: Intersections of subspaces are subspaces
primary_statement: An arbitrary intersection of subspaces is a subspace; a union of two subspaces is a subspace only if one contains the other

title: Linear combination
primary_statement: A finite sum sum_{i=1}^k a_i v_i with a_i in F and v_i in V

title: Span
primary_statement: span(S) is the set of all finite linear combinations of elements of S: the smallest subspace containing S. span(empty) = {0}

title: Span is the smallest containing subspace
primary_statement: span(S) is a subspace and is contained in every subspace containing S

title: Linear independence
primary_statement: (v_i) is independent iff the only finite linear combination of them equal to 0 has all coefficients 0

title: Linear dependence lemma
primary_statement: If (v_1,...,v_k) is dependent and v_1 != 0 then some v_j lies in span(v_1,...,v_{j-1}); removing it does not change the span

title: Basis
primary_statement: A linearly independent spanning set. Defined without reference to any number, so that dimension can be proved well-defined

title: Steinitz exchange lemma
primary_statement: If (u_1,...,u_m) is independent and (w_1,...,w_n) spans V then m <= n, and the u's can be exchanged into the spanning list

title: Every finitely generated space has a basis
primary_statement: A finite spanning set contains a basis and every independent set extends to a basis. Choice-free

title: Every vector space has a basis (Zorn)
primary_statement: Every vector space has a basis. Equivalent to the axiom of choice over ZF

title: Any two bases are equinumerous
primary_statement: Any two bases of a finitely generated vector space have the same number of elements

title: Dimension
primary_statement: dim V is the common cardinality of any basis of V; dim {0} = 0

title: Subspace dimension
primary_statement: If U is a subspace of finite-dimensional V then dim U <= dim V, with equality iff U = V

title: Unique representation in a basis
primary_statement: B is a basis iff every v in V is a unique finite linear combination of elements of B

title: Ordered basis and coordinates
primary_statement: An ordered basis B = (b_1,...,b_n) gives the coordinate map [.]_B : V -> F^n, a linear bijection

title: Every n-dimensional space is isomorphic to F^n
primary_statement: dim V = n implies V is isomorphic to F^n via coordinates; the isomorphism depends on the chosen basis

title: Sum of subspaces
primary_statement: U + W = {u + w : u in U, w in W}, the smallest subspace containing both

title: Direct sum
primary_statement: V = U (+) W iff V = U + W and U ∩ W = {0}; equivalently every v decomposes uniquely as u + w

title: Dimension of a sum (Grassmann formula)
primary_statement: dim(U + W) = dim U + dim W - dim(U ∩ W) for finite-dimensional U and W

title: Quotient space V/U
primary_statement: V/U with (v + U) + (w + U) = (v + w) + U and a(v + U) = av + U; well-defined because U is a subspace

title: dim(V/U) = dim V - dim U
primary_statement: For finite-dimensional V and a subspace U, dim(V/U) = dim V - dim U

title: Linear map
primary_statement: T: V -> W with T(au + bv) = aT(u) + bT(v) for all a,b in F and u,v in V

title: A linear map is determined by its values on a basis
primary_statement: Given a basis (b_i) of V and any (w_i) in W there is exactly one linear T with T(b_i) = w_i

title: Kernel (null space)
primary_statement: ker T = {v in V : T(v) = 0}, a subspace of V

title: Image (range)
primary_statement: im T = T(V) = {T(v) : v in V}, a subspace of W

title: T injective iff ker T = {0}
primary_statement: A linear map is injective exactly when its kernel is the zero subspace

title: Rank of a linear map
primary_statement: rank T = dim(im T). Defined without the determinant, breaking the rank-determinant cycle

title: Nullity
primary_statement: nullity T = dim(ker T)

title: Rank-nullity theorem
primary_statement: For T: V -> W with V finite-dimensional, dim V = rank T + nullity T

title: On equal finite dimensions injective iff surjective
primary_statement: If dim V = dim W < infinity then T: V -> W is injective iff surjective iff bijective. Fails without finite-dimensionality

title: Isomorphism
primary_statement: A bijective linear map; its set-inverse is automatically linear

title: First isomorphism theorem
primary_statement: V/ker T is isomorphic to im T via v + ker T  maps to  T(v)

title: The space L(V,W)
primary_statement: L(V,W) is a vector space under pointwise operations; dim L(V,W) = (dim V)(dim W) in finite dimension

title: Composition is linear and bilinear
primary_statement: The composite of linear maps is linear; composition is associative and bilinear over L

title: Linear operator
primary_statement: A linear map from V to itself; L(V) is an associative algebra under composition

title: Invertible operator
primary_statement: T in L(V) with a two-sided inverse in L(V); in finite dimension a one-sided inverse suffices

title: Dual space
primary_statement: V^* = L(V, F), the space of linear functionals on V

title: Dual basis
primary_statement: A basis (b_1,...,b_n) of finite-dimensional V yields a basis (b_1^*,...,b_n^*) of V^* with b_i^*(b_j) = delta_{ij}; hence dim V^* = dim V

title: Dual (transpose) map
primary_statement: T^t: W^* -> V^* with T^t(g) = g o T; its matrix in dual bases is the transpose of the matrix of T

title: Canonical isomorphism V to V^**
primary_statement: Evaluation v  maps to  (f  maps to  f(v)) is injective always and an isomorphism when dim V is finite. Basis-independent, unlike V to V^*

title: Annihilator of a subspace
primary_statement: U^0 = {f in V^* : f(u) = 0 for all u in U}; dim U + dim U^0 = dim V in finite dimension

title: Matrix
primary_statement: A in F^{m x n} is a function {1..m} x {1..n} -> F, written as a rectangular array

title: Matrix addition and scalar multiplication
primary_statement: Entrywise operations making F^{m x n} a vector space of dimension mn

title: Matrix multiplication
primary_statement: (AB)_{ij} = sum_k A_{ik} B_{kj}, defined when the inner shapes agree

title: Matrix product represents composition
primary_statement: [S o T]_{D<-B} = [S]_{D<-C} [T]_{C<-B}; associativity of the matrix product follows from associativity of composition

title: Matrix multiplication is not commutative
primary_statement: AB != BA in general, with a 2x2 witness. Every identity manipulated as if the entries were scalars is suspect

title: Transpose
primary_statement: (A^T)_{ij} = A_{ji}; (AB)^T = B^T A^T and (A^T)^T = A

title: Conjugate transpose
primary_statement: (A^*)_{ij} = conj(A_{ji}); over R it is the transpose. The correct adjoint for the complex inner product

title: Identity matrix
primary_statement: I_n with (I_n)_{ij} = delta_{ij}, the multiplicative identity of F^{n x n}

title: Invertible matrix
primary_statement: A in F^{n x n} with AB = BA = I for some B; the inverse is unique and (AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}

title: One-sided inverses of square matrices are two-sided
primary_statement: For square A over a field, AB = I implies BA = I. Fails for non-square A and in infinite dimension

title: Elementary row operations
primary_statement: Row swap, scaling a row by a nonzero scalar, and adding a multiple of one row to another

title: Elementary matrices
primary_statement: Each elementary row operation is left multiplication by an invertible elementary matrix

title: Row equivalence
primary_statement: A ~_r B iff B = EA for a product E of elementary matrices; preserves the row space and the null space

title: Row echelon and reduced row echelon form
primary_statement: Leading entries strictly rightward down the rows, zero rows last; RREF additionally has leading 1s that are the only nonzero entry in their column

title: The RREF of a matrix is unique
primary_statement: Every matrix is row equivalent to exactly one matrix in reduced row echelon form

title: Gaussian elimination
primary_statement: Reduction to row echelon form by elementary operations, O(n^3) for n x n; solves Ax = b and computes rank and the inverse

title: Pivot and free columns
primary_statement: Pivot columns of the RREF index a basis of the column space of A; free columns parameterise the null space

title: Row space
primary_statement: The span of the rows of A, a subspace of F^n, invariant under row operations

title: Column space
primary_statement: The span of the columns of A; equals the image of x  maps to  Ax

title: Null space
primary_statement: {x : Ax = 0}, the kernel of x  maps to  Ax

title: Left null space
primary_statement: {y : A^T y = 0}, the null space of A^T

title: The four fundamental subspaces
primary_statement: row(A) and null(A) live in F^n with dimensions r and n-r; col(A) and null(A^T) in F^m with dimensions r and m-r. Orthogonality of the pairs needs an inner product

title: Row rank equals column rank
primary_statement: dim row(A) = dim col(A) = rank A, over any field

title: Rank of a matrix
primary_statement: rank A = dim col(A); equals the number of pivots in any row echelon form of A

title: Rank inequalities
primary_statement: rank(AB) <= min(rank A, rank B); rank(A+B) <= rank A + rank B; Sylvester: rank(AB) >= rank A + rank B - n

title: Equivalent characterisations of invertibility
primary_statement: For square A: invertible iff rank n iff null(A) = {0} iff RREF is I iff a product of elementary matrices iff det A != 0 iff 0 is not an eigenvalue

title: Linear system Ax = b
primary_statement: Ax = b is consistent iff b is in col(A); its solution set is x_p + null(A), an affine subspace

title: LU factorisation
primary_statement: A = LU with L unit lower triangular and U upper triangular when no pivoting is required; PA = LU in general

title: When LU needs pivoting
primary_statement: LU without row interchanges exists iff every leading principal minor is nonzero; partial pivoting is needed otherwise and for numerical stability

title: Block matrices
primary_statement: Partitioned matrices multiply blockwise when the partitions are conformable

title: Schur complement
primary_statement: For M = [[A,B],[C,D]] with A invertible, the Schur complement is D - C A^{-1} B, and det M = det A * det(D - CA^{-1}B)

title: Trace
primary_statement: tr(A) = sum_i A_{ii}, a linear functional on F^{n x n}

title: Trace is cyclic and similarity-invariant
primary_statement: tr(AB) = tr(BA), hence tr(P^{-1}AP) = tr(A): trace is a property of the operator, not the basis

title: Triangular and diagonal matrices
primary_statement: Upper and lower triangular and diagonal matrices; closed under products, invertible iff no diagonal entry is zero

title: Matrix of a linear map
primary_statement: [T]_{C<-B} has as its j-th column the C-coordinates of T(b_j), which makes [S o T] = [S][T]

title: Change of basis
primary_statement: [T]_{B'} = P^{-1} [T]_B P where P is the change-of-basis matrix

title: Similarity
primary_statement: A ~ B iff B = P^{-1} A P for some invertible P; an equivalence relation whose classes are the operators up to choice of basis

title: Permutations and sign
primary_statement: S_n and the sign homomorphism sgn: S_n -> {+1,-1}, well-defined by the parity of any decomposition into transpositions

title: Multilinear alternating form
primary_statement: D: (F^n)^n -> F linear in each column and zero whenever two columns are equal

title: Determinant
primary_statement: det is the unique multilinear alternating function of the columns with det(I) = 1. Defined without eigenvalues, breaking the det-eigenvalue cycle

title: Existence and uniqueness of the determinant
primary_statement: There is exactly one normalised alternating multilinear form on the columns of F^{n x n}

title: Leibniz formula
primary_statement: det A = sum_{sigma in S_n} sgn(sigma) prod_i A_{i,sigma(i)}. A theorem here, not the definition

title: Determinant under row operations
primary_statement: A row swap negates det; scaling a row by c scales det by c; adding a multiple of a row leaves det unchanged

title: Determinant of a triangular matrix
primary_statement: The determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of its diagonal entries

title: det(A^T) = det(A)
primary_statement: The determinant is unchanged by transposition, so every row statement has a column counterpart

title: det(AB) = det(A)det(B)
primary_statement: The determinant is multiplicative over any field

title: det A != 0 iff A is invertible
primary_statement: A square matrix over a field is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero; then det(A^{-1}) = 1/det(A)

title: Cofactor (Laplace) expansion
primary_statement: det A = sum_j (-1)^{i+j} A_{ij} M_{ij} along any row i, and likewise along any column

title: Adjugate and the inverse formula
primary_statement: adj(A)_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} M_{ji}; A adj(A) = adj(A) A = det(A) I, so A^{-1} = adj(A)/det(A) when det A != 0

title: Cramer's rule
primary_statement: For invertible A the unique solution of Ax = b has x_i = det(A_i)/det(A), where A_i replaces column i of A by b

title: Determinant is similarity-invariant
primary_statement: det(P^{-1}AP) = det(A), so det is a property of the operator

title: Rank via minors
primary_statement: rank A is the largest r such that some r x r minor of A is nonzero. A theorem, not the definition of rank

title: Determinant as a signed volume factor
primary_statement: Over R, the absolute value of det A is the factor by which A scales n-dimensional volume, and its sign records orientation

title: Vandermonde determinant
primary_statement: The Vandermonde determinant on x_1..x_n is prod_{i<j}(x_j - x_i), nonzero iff the nodes are distinct

title: Eigenvalue and eigenvector
primary_statement: lambda in F is an eigenvalue of T if Tv = lambda v for some v != 0; such a v is an eigenvector. Defined without the determinant

title: Eigenspace
primary_statement: E_lambda = ker(T - lambda I), consisting of 0 and the eigenvectors for lambda

title: Characteristic polynomial
primary_statement: p_A(t) = det(tI - A), monic of degree n and a similarity invariant

title: Eigenvalues are exactly the roots of the characteristic polynomial
primary_statement: lambda is an eigenvalue of A iff p_A(lambda) = 0. The theorem linking the two independent definitions

title: Trace and determinant from the characteristic polynomial
primary_statement: p_A(t) = t^n - tr(A)t^{n-1} + ... + (-1)^n det(A); when p_A splits, tr is the sum and det the product of the eigenvalues with multiplicity

title: Every operator on a nonzero space over a closed field has an eigenvalue
primary_statement: Over an algebraically closed field every operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional space has an eigenvalue. Fails over R

title: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are independent
primary_statement: Eigenvectors belonging to pairwise distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent

title: Algebraic and geometric multiplicity
primary_statement: Algebraic multiplicity is the multiplicity as a root of p_A, geometric is dim E_lambda; always geometric <= algebraic

title: Diagonalisable operator
primary_statement: T is diagonalisable if some basis of V consists of eigenvectors, equivalently A = PDP^{-1} with D diagonal

title: Diagonalisability criterion
primary_statement: T is diagonalisable iff p_T splits and every eigenvalue's geometric multiplicity equals its algebraic multiplicity, equivalently V is the direct sum of the eigenspaces

title: n distinct eigenvalues implies diagonalisable
primary_statement: An n x n matrix with n distinct eigenvalues in F is diagonalisable. Sufficient, not necessary

title: A non-diagonalisable matrix
primary_statement: [[1,1],[0,1]] has p(t) = (t-1)^2 but a one-dimensional eigenspace; the defect is geometric < algebraic multiplicity

title: Minimal polynomial
primary_statement: The monic generator m_T of the ideal of polynomials annihilating T; it divides every annihilating polynomial

title: Cayley-Hamilton theorem
primary_statement: Every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial: p_A(A) = 0

title: Diagonalisable iff the minimal polynomial has distinct linear factors
primary_statement: T is diagonalisable iff m_T splits into distinct linear factors over F

title: Invariant subspace
primary_statement: U with T(U) contained in U; the restriction is an operator on U and its minimal polynomial divides m_T

title: Schur triangularisation
primary_statement: Over C every square matrix is unitarily similar to an upper triangular matrix: A = QTQ^*

title: Nilpotent operator
primary_statement: N with N^k = 0 for some k; its only eigenvalue is 0 and N^{dim V} = 0

title: Generalised eigenspace
primary_statement: G_lambda = ker((T - lambda I)^{dim V}); its dimension is the algebraic multiplicity of lambda

title: Primary decomposition
primary_statement: If p_T splits, V is the direct sum of the generalised eigenspaces and T acts on each as lambda I plus a nilpotent

title: Jordan normal form (stated)
primary_statement: Over an algebraically closed field every operator has a basis in which its matrix is block diagonal with Jordan blocks, unique up to block order. STATED, not proved in Release 0.1

title: Similarity invariants
primary_statement: Similar matrices share rank, trace, determinant, characteristic polynomial, minimal polynomial, and eigenvalue multiplicities; the characteristic polynomial alone does not determine similarity

title: Inner product
primary_statement: A positive-definite form on V over R or C, linear in the first slot and conjugate-symmetric, with <v,v> > 0 for v != 0

title: Inner product space
primary_statement: A vector space over R or C equipped with an inner product

title: Induced norm
primary_statement: The norm ||v|| = sqrt(<v,v>): positive definite, absolutely homogeneous, and subadditive

title: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
primary_statement: The absolute value of <u,v> is at most ||u|| ||v||, with equality iff u and v are linearly dependent

title: Triangle inequality
primary_statement: u + v|| <= ||u|| + ||v||, a consequence of Cauchy-Schwarz

title: Parallelogram law
primary_statement: u+v||^2 + ||u-v||^2 = 2||u||^2 + 2||v||^2; characterises the norms that come from an inner product

title: Polarisation identity
primary_statement: The inner product is recovered from the norm; the real form needs a factor 1/2, hence characteristic not 2

title: Orthogonality
primary_statement: u perp v iff <u,v> = 0; a set is orthogonal if its elements are pairwise orthogonal

title: Pythagorean theorem
primary_statement: If u perp v then ||u+v||^2 = ||u||^2 + ||v||^2; over C the converse needs only the real part of <u,v> to vanish

title: An orthogonal set of nonzero vectors is independent
primary_statement: Pairwise orthogonality plus nonvanishing forces linear independence

title: Orthonormal set and basis
primary_statement: Pairwise orthogonal unit vectors; an orthonormal basis gives coordinates by <v, e_i> with no matrix inversion

title: Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation
primary_statement: Converts an independent list into an orthonormal list with the same successive spans, so every finite-dimensional inner product space has an orthonormal basis

title: Bessel's inequality
primary_statement: The sum of the squared coefficients over any orthonormal set is at most ||v||^2

title: Parseval's identity
primary_statement: For an orthonormal BASIS, ||v||^2 equals the sum of the squared coefficients, and the inner product is the coefficient inner product

title: Orthogonal complement
primary_statement: U^perp = {v : <v,u> = 0 for all u in U}, a subspace; U^perp = (span U)^perp

title: Orthogonal decomposition theorem
primary_statement: For a finite-dimensional subspace U, V = U (+) U^perp and (U^perp)^perp = U

title: Orthogonal projection onto a subspace
primary_statement: P_U v = sum_i <v, e_i> e_i for an orthonormal basis (e_i) of U, independent of which orthonormal basis is chosen

title: A matrix is an orthogonal projection iff P^2 = P = P^T
primary_statement: Over R, P represents orthogonal projection onto col(P) exactly when P is idempotent and symmetric. The result math-statistics uses for the hat matrix

title: Best approximation theorem
primary_statement: P_U v is the unique closest point of U to v: ||v - P_U v|| < ||v - u|| for every other u in U

title: Least squares and the normal equations
primary_statement: A minimiser of ||Ax - b|| is exactly a solution of A^T A x = A^T b, unique iff A has full column rank, and then x = (A^TA)^{-1}A^Tb

title: The hat matrix H = A(A^TA)^{-1}A^T
primary_statement: H is the orthogonal projection onto col(A): symmetric, idempotent, of rank equal to rank A, with tr(H) = rank A

title: QR factorisation
primary_statement: A = QR with Q having orthonormal columns and R upper triangular, from Gram-Schmidt on the columns; solves least squares without forming A^TA

title: Adjoint of a linear map
primary_statement: The unique T^* with <Tv, w> = <v, T^*w>; its matrix in orthonormal bases is the conjugate transpose

title: ker(T^*) = (im T)^perp
primary_statement: The four fundamental subspaces form two orthogonal pairs: null(A) = row(A)^perp and null(A^T) = col(A)^perp

title: Self-adjoint (symmetric, Hermitian)
primary_statement: T = T^*; over R, A = A^T. The class for which the real spectral theorem holds

title: Orthogonal and unitary matrices
primary_statement: Q^TQ = I over R and U^*U = I over C; equivalently the columns are orthonormal and the map preserves the inner product

title: Norm-preserving iff inner-product-preserving iff unitary
primary_statement: For a linear map on a finite-dimensional inner product space, preserving the norm, preserving the inner product, and U^*U = I are equivalent

title: Normal matrix
primary_statement: AA^* = A^*A; contains the self-adjoint, skew-adjoint, and unitary matrices

title: A self-adjoint operator has real eigenvalues
primary_statement: Every eigenvalue of a self-adjoint operator is real, and eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal

title: Spectral theorem for real symmetric matrices
primary_statement: A real symmetric A has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors: A = Q D Q^T with Q orthogonal and D real diagonal

title: Spectral theorem for normal matrices
primary_statement: Over C, A is unitarily diagonalisable iff A is normal: A = U D U^*

title: Spectral decomposition as a sum of projections
primary_statement: A self-adjoint A equals the sum over distinct eigenvalues of lambda_i P_i with P_i the orthogonal projections onto the eigenspaces, P_iP_j = 0 and sum P_i = I

title: Rayleigh quotient
primary_statement: R(x) = <Ax,x>/<x,x> for x != 0. A DEFINITION only: that its extrema over the unit sphere are the extreme eigenvalues is proved downstream (see courant_fischer), which is what keeps it usable inside the spectral theorem's own proof

title: Courant-Fischer min-max theorem
primary_statement: Each eigenvalue is a min-max of the Rayleigh quotient over subspaces of fixed dimension; yields eigenvalue interlacing under rank-one and submatrix perturbation

title: Quadratic form
primary_statement: q(x) = x^T A x with A symmetric; the symmetric A is unique when the characteristic is not 2

title: Congruence of symmetric matrices
primary_statement: A ~_c B iff B = P^T A P with P invertible: the change-of-variable relation for quadratic forms, distinct from similarity

title: Positive definite matrix
primary_statement: Symmetric A with x^T A x > 0 for every x != 0; positive semidefinite if the inequality is not strict

title: Equivalent characterisations of positive definiteness
primary_statement: For real symmetric A: positive definite iff all eigenvalues positive iff all leading principal minors positive (Sylvester's criterion) iff A = B^TB with B of full column rank iff A has a Cholesky factorisation

title: Gram matrix
primary_statement: G_{ij} = <v_i, v_j> is positive semidefinite, positive definite iff the v_i are independent, and rank G = dim span(v_i)

title: Cholesky factorisation
primary_statement: A positive definite real symmetric A factors uniquely as A = LL^T with L lower triangular with positive diagonal

title: Sylvester's law of inertia
primary_statement: The numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix are invariant under congruence; the signature classifies real quadratic forms

title: Simultaneous diagonalisation
primary_statement: Two real symmetric matrices with one positive definite are simultaneously diagonalisable by congruence; two normal matrices are simultaneously unitarily diagonalisable iff they commute

title: Singular value decomposition
primary_statement: Every A in F^{m x n} factors as A = U Sigma V^* with U and V unitary and Sigma diagonal with nonnegative nonincreasing entries

title: Singular values
primary_statement: The nonnegative square roots of the eigenvalues of A^*A; rank A is the number of nonzero singular values

title: SVD bases for the four fundamental subspaces
primary_statement: The first r columns of U and V give orthonormal bases of col(A) and row(A); the remaining columns give null(A^T) and null(A)

title: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse
primary_statement: A^+ = V Sigma^+ U^*, the unique matrix satisfying the four Penrose conditions; A^+b is the minimum-norm least-squares solution

title: Eckart-Young low-rank approximation
primary_statement: The best rank-k approximation to A in the spectral and Frobenius norms is the truncated SVD, with errors sigma_{k+1} and the root-sum-of-squares of the discarded singular values

title: Operator and Frobenius norms
primary_statement: A||_2 = sigma_1 and ||A||_F = sqrt(tr(A^*A)) = root-sum-of-squares of the singular values; both submultiplicative

title: Condition number
primary_statement: kappa_2(A) = sigma_1/sigma_n bounds relative error amplification in solving Ax = b. A large kappa means ill-conditioned, not singular

title: Spectral radius
primary_statement: rho(A) = max of the absolute values of the eigenvalues; rho(A) <= ||A|| for every submultiplicative norm, with equality for normal A in the spectral norm

title: Where finite-dimensionality is load-bearing
primary_statement: A catalogue of results that fail in infinite dimension: rank-nullity, injective-iff-surjective, V isomorphic to V^**, existence of an eigenvalue, and a basis-free adjoint. STATED

title: Modules over a PID (stated)
primary_statement: Over a PID every finitely generated module is a direct sum of cyclic modules; the common home of the Jordan and Smith normal forms. STATED, out of scope
